key_insight: Combining physics-based simulation with neural networks identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports process-window selection for robust HDPE joints by predicting thermal response, axial forces and defect formation.
method: Simulate material flow, temperature, force and defects using a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model.
Train two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force data.
Use CEL–ANN predictions to map defective and defect-free welding windows.
evidence_signal: Experimental validation showed good CEL agreement, ANN R² values of 0.91–0.99, and a peak plunge-force reduction from 1600 N to about 1100 N with 60 °C preheating.
watch_item: Predictive performance is established within the tested process space; new tool geometries, HDPE grades or operating ranges require further validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
